record.what_it_does: Airtable is a cloud database/spreadsheet-hybrid platform whose API lets external systems read and write bases, tables, records, fields, and webhooks.
record.auth_notes: Airtable calls its static bearer token a 'personal access token' (PAT), created at airtable.com/create/tokens and passed as an Authorization: Bearer header; it acts as the creating user's own account and is meant for personal/internal integrations. For any integration where third-party users grant access, Airtable explicitly directs developers to use OAuth2 (registered at airtable.com/create/oauth), which also issues Bearer-style access tokens via the standard OAuth grant flow. Legacy API keys were fully deprecated as of Feb 1, 2024.
record.access_notes: Any developer can sign up for a free Airtable account and immediately generate a personal access token or register an OAuth integration with no cost gate; API access itself is not paywalled ('Billing plans: All plans' on endpoints), though sharing an OAuth integration publicly requires adding a privacy policy/TOS URL (no approval/review process, just profile completeness).

evidence.quote: We currently support using personal access tokens and OAuth access tokens during the authentication process.
Any integrations that allow other users to grant access to Airtable should use OAuth.
Authentication: Personal access token, OAuth integration
The personal access tokens panel can be accessed at /create/tokens. Here, you can create new tokens and manage your existing tokens.
The API closely follows REST semantics, uses JSON to encode objects, and relies on standard HTTP codes to signal operation outcomes.
Lists all webhooks that are registered for a base, along with their statuses.
Airtable's MCP server lets you connect AI tools directly to your Airtable bases.

record.open_questions: No official OpenAPI/Swagger spec was located on the public docs site (only the interactive reference and airtable.js client are listed), so openapi_spec is left null rather than asserted false.
